headline: Operating earnings jump under Abel · investment marks weigh
summary_short: Berkshire's operating earnings rose 17.7% y/y to $11.35B in Q1 2026, the first quarter under Greg Abel as CEO. Insurance underwriting and BNSF led the gains. Net earnings of $10.11B benefited from smaller investment mark-to-market losses versus a large drag in Q1 2025.
summary_long: Operating earnings advanced across all major segments except insurance-investment income (which declined slightly on lower yields). Insurance underwriting was the standout at $1.72B (+28.5% y/y) as the P&C portfolio benefited from favorable prior-year reserve development. BNSF operating earnings rose 13.4% to $1.38B on volume gains. Berkshire Hathaway Energy was roughly flat at $1.11B. Net earnings of $10.11B were more than 2× Q1 2025 primarily because investment mark-to-market losses shrank to -$1.24B from -$5.04B a year earlier. Insurance float grew to ~$176.9B (+$500M from year-end 2025). Foreign-currency effects contributed +$249M in Q1 2026 vs -$713M in Q1 2025. Q1 2026 is Greg Abel's first quarter as Berkshire CEO following Warren Buffett's transition to Chairman.

drivers.explanation: Broad-based segment gains led by insurance underwriting (+28.5%) and BNSF (+13.4%); Insurance-investment income was a slight offset.
Investment mark-to-market losses shrank to -$1.24B from -$5.04B in Q1 2025; foreign-currency effects flipped from -$713M loss to +$249M gain.
Favorable prior-year reserve development and premium growth across the P&C book.

confidence_notes: Filing-based summary from Exhibit 99.1 of the May 7 2026 8-K. All KPI values sourced from the earnings press release. Y/Y deltas as disclosed. Operating earnings excludes investment gains/losses per Berkshire's disclosure convention; net earnings is GAAP-reported including mark-to-market. Q2 2026 10-Q had not been filed with SEC as of 2026-08-04.
